“Do not be afraid, I Am!”

Article in which Fr. Buela comments on Mt 14:27 I – When you see the boat of the Church buffeted by contrary winds in the midst of the raging sea… – When you see the waves, furious and foaming, strike the keel and sweep over the gunwale… – When the black clouds of evil darken the atmosphere, making the air unbreathable… – When the roar of the thunder of selfishness deafens men throughout the whole world in violence, wars, destruction and death… – When the blazing lightning of hatred turns the face of the earth into a Dantesque scene… – When you see the young grown old before their time because they have let themselves be enslaved by disordered passions… – When you see adults as if dazed, unable to find their way… – When television, radio, newspapers and magazines are hotbeds of immorality and corruption… – When failed marriages and broken families are daily news… – When newly conceived children are killed with impunity… – When one is tormented by difficulties, temptations, misunderstandings, persecutions… – When the epidemic of materialism creeps through the bowels of humanity… – When, having to stake everything for Christ, you feel dizzy at the thought of what He might ask of you… I Am! II Who is this I? Second Person of the Most Holy Trinity announced by the prophets born in Bethlehem died on the Cross rose on the third day… III Exodus 3:14 I Am… Before Abraham was :… (Jn 8,) the Way, the Truth, the Life (Jn 14:6) the Resurrection (Jn 11:25) the living bread come down from heaven (Jn 6:41) the light of the world (Jn 8:12) the door (Jn 10:9) the good shepherd (Jn 10:11) the true life (Jn 15:1) the alpha and the omega, the First and the Last, the one who is coming (Rev 1:17) .
Age quod agis

Good-night talk of Fr. Buela at the Major Seminary “Mary, Mother of the Incarnate Word” I am going to take up again a custom I had in the early years. It was a sort of “good night” on very particular topics –which often are not topics suited to a sermon, but even so always bear much fruit–, and I used to give it always at the beginning of the academic year. The first thing I want to talk about today: we would accomplish nothing good if we do not manage to form young men who know how to be authentically free. To be authentically free, one has to know how to be disciplined; otherwise, under the pretext of freedom, one seeks oneself, and that is not true freedom. It is not enough for one simply to fulfill outwardly the things one has to fulfill, the things one has to do; rather, there has to be a deep conviction and there has to be a formation of habits. Good habits, so that later in priestly life (I am thinking, for example, of parish life, where one is practically “besieged” all day long) the priest may know how to attend to the things he must attend to, and give time to the important things to which he has to give time. The thing is this: you will not succeed in forming an authentically free young man, an authentically disciplined young man, a young man who knows how to make good use of his time, if he is not taught, in no uncertain terms, to get up early. When you see a seminary where there is practically no set time for getting up; if one does not get up at the time one has to get up, afterwards one will not be able to put anything in order. I know cases of some consecrated persons who habitually get up late, and their whole day is crooked; they do not have time even to do the fundamental things. Let alone doing some “little thing more,” no. To get up early you have to go to bed early, there is “no way around it.” As a priest one may sometimes go to bed late, but two days, three days, four days… in the end that priest ends up getting up late. And what suffers? Prayer suffers. Here, in the seminary, what suffers? The next day’s Mass! Someone might think himself “clever” for going to bed late, but the next day he is asleep. Who suffers? The most important thing we have in the day suffers, which is the Mass. Look: –it will have happened to you when you were university students or were in the world; generally when one is in the world one leads a very disorderly life– many go to bed late because they think they gain time that way, but the time they gain at night they lose in the morning. We consecrated souls are delicate flowers; if we do not have method, we die. And there is no way to have method if one does not go to bed early. The English have a saying: “Early to bed and early to raise, makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise” (“Going to bed early and getting up early makes a man healthy, rich and wise”). That is why, when there is a fixed schedule –which is set by the superiors, which means that the time for going to bed is a studied and tested schedule–, it must be respected; one must go to bed at that time. One cannot appeal to “freedom of spirit” in order to go to bed at any hour. No! Because this is one of the points that must be very clear. If one does not rest enough, what happens in many seminaries happens: they start with stress, or some other similar or related thing. Of course, they have to study, so they stay up at night to study. No, it is better to go to bed at the proper time and, with the permission of the proper person, to get up earlier if one is in a hurry, if one has something urgent; and if not, to sleep with complete peace of mind the hours God gave us for that. Because that Latin apothegm is also very true: “Age quod agis” (do what you are doing). Whoever turns day into night and night into day lives a life upside down. And so, if one has to sleep, then one must sleep; I sanctify myself at this moment by doing what I have to do: sleep. Not study: sleep; and when it is time to study, study. “Age quod agis .” And to Mass, which is the most important thing, come well prepared; and if I get up half asleep: give my head a good soaking –beforehand– with cold water. Mass is the most important thing, and I must prepare myself. I do not know whether you notice it, but one –perhaps it is the years– prepares oneself for the great feasts we have in the Seminary. For example, when it is the feast of the Incarnate Word, does the feast arrive unexpectedly ? No; one gradually prepares, one prepares the soul to enjoy, to delight in the Mass, the greetings, the celebration. The same must be done with the daily Mass. When one arrives at the church it seems that the heart begins to beat faster. One thought on any aspect of the Eucharistic mystery is enough for one to profit from the whole Mass. And all the more in these difficult times. We have to pray for peace in Zaire, for peace in Albania, for peace in the places where people go on killing one another like flies. But if the religious does not dispose his soul, if he wastes that moment which is the most important of the day, afterwards, when he is a priest –if he gets to be a priest– he will not know how to profit from the daily Mass. So remember: I must make good use of time; I cannot make good use of time if I do not order my life, and I do not order my life if I do not go to bed early. You should even know that at some point you may need to sleep a little more: then go to bed earlier. Here there is noise because afterwards a battalion comes in, but one is already in bed, one is settling down. One can also make up for it by sleeping a little longer at siesta time, by going to bed earlier. Nothing is gained by having stressed, nervous people, who afterwards start to suffer from surmenage . I have seen very gifted young men in seminaries –I am thinking at this moment of a splendid young man who foolishly fell into surmenage , and was left in a bad way for the rest of the journey: his preaching is a “watering can,” one never knows when it is going to end. The intellect is left as if wounded, as if injured, and so it loses the brilliance it had before. Let us learn to be faithful “in small things,” as the Gospel says, and so we will come to be faithful “in great things.” We would accomplish nothing good if we do not manage to form young men who know how to be authentically free. To be authentically free, one has to know how to be disciplined.
The mother

Homily preached by Rev. Fr. Carlos M. Buela, I.V.E., at the Youth Mass on Sunday, October 15, Mother’s Day, and at the Holy Mass for the family, celebrated for the children of the «Isabel la Católica» School and for their parents, on October 20, 1995 We are gathered to celebrate the Holy Mass for the Family. A few days ago, on October 12, we recalled the example of that great woman of whom it can be said that she changed the course of history, a woman who stood out as a Christian, as a wife, as a mother and as a queen: Isabella the Catholic! Today I want to speak about the one who is the soul of every family, the mother 1 . A Hindu legend tells that when God wanted to create a mother, He thought long about how to make her… From the reed He took slenderness, from the grasses their gentle trembling, from the petal of the rose its enchanting velvety softness. From the rays of the sun He took joy, from fire its heartfelt warmth, from the clouds tears, and the confiding chatter of turtledoves. With all these exquisite things He formed the mother. That is why sorrow nests in her soul, for there is nothing more vulnerable than the breath of the rose, nor more timid than the trembling of the grass. Weakness, however, turns into strength in her. The mother, all sweetness, becomes fiercer than a hyena when she has to defend her children. The mother is the guardian angel of our childhood! The soul trembles and the heart beats faster when we say the word: MOTHER! Who does not feel tears well up in their eyes when thinking of the one who has never stopped loving them from the first instant of their life, the one who smiled -like a sun- over the cradle, the one who wept and grieved when her little child fell ill and had to suffer? 1. What is a mother? Who can say what it means to be a mother? If we gathered together everything that has been written about her, the songs that speak of the mother in the home, the sighs that rise from the hearts of orphans in the cemetery… If we could see through to the torn soul of the mother speaking with her wayward son through the bars of a prison, if it were possible for us to count the hours a mother spends keeping watch beside the bed of her sick child, if we managed to call to mind the proud figure of the mother of the Gracchi, the tears of St. Monica, the loving heart of Blanche of Castile, the fortitude of the mother of the Maccabees, the incomparable spiritual stature of Isabella the Catholic, the piety of Mamma Margaret, or that of the modest woman who works day and night to support her family, and, above all, if we set before us the eminent figure of the Most Holy Virgin, Mother of God… we would have only a faint inkling of what a mother is! Do you know what a mother is? She is the mirror of the soul who is always at our side! My mom is elderly now, she is 85, but she still cooks, washes the dishes, works… all with great joy. When I was in the Seminary, once, 25 years ago, she wrote me the following in a letter: “Carlitos: You write to us so that we may share your joys and emotions, but even if you had not explained your satisfactions to us, I am always at your side; this brought back to me the memory of a reading from when I was in 3rd grade, which stayed ‘in mente’: «My son, if you look at yourself in the mirror of your bedroom, you will see yourself as you are, with a smiling or a sad little face, and so… your dear little mother laughs if you laugh, cries if you cry… because she is the mirror of your soul…». That is what a mother is! The mirror of our soul! The one who is always at our side, beside us! 2. The most beautiful reality A mother cannot be enclosed in intellectual categories. She is not to be understood, but loved. Her kisses, the tears that spring from her eyes, her prayer, tell you what a mother is… Mother, dear mother! How much these words say! A spellbinding power throbs in them. A sweet word that sounds like a lament, like the sound of a distant and mysterious bugle, it produces a joyful tingling in our heart, and when we pronounce it, our whole soul vibrates on our lips. Is there any creature to whom we are more united, in heart and soul, than to our mother? For nine months we lived beneath her heart! After God, the greatest grace and the greatest good we possess is our mother. The word mother! speaks to us of admirable acts of perseverance, of goodness, of love, of sacrifice. 3. Her work The mother gives us life, holds us close to her heart, looks at us with tenderness, teaches us to speak, to love, to laugh, to walk. When we are little she feeds us with her own substance; she gives us bread when we are older. She takes care of us, protects us, warms us with the warmth of her own heart. Her love has no boundaries. She can generously give up her own interests and suffer with a smile on her lips because she loves; she is capable of renouncing, out of love for her child, all the grandeurs of the earth. She devotes her life to struggling for her children and rejoices to see them happy. A good mother is a blessing from God and the supreme consolation that has been given us in this valley of tears. She shows us the way when we go astray. She lifts us up when we fall. She encourages us when we are downcast. She sweetens life on earth and, as if by magic, turns thorns into roses. God transmits to the world the consolation of love through the soul of the mother. As a poet said: A mother’s hands carved out of oak lined with silk that suffer joyfully that pray in silence. That work so much that caress so gently that educate so firmly that rest so little. A mother’s hands that live loving that sweetly, so sweetly die forgiving… I kiss them, I kiss them a thousand times, praying; blessed forever be the hands of mothers. The mother comes from God and is one of the most adorable and moving divine revelations. We cannot help being moved when we consider this marvel of God, and praising God for having placed His love in the heart of the mother. Throughout history we can see the endless series of mothers who pass the torch of life from hand to hand, a torch that will one day return to the bosom of God, from whence it first came forth. Dear brothers and sisters: * Those who no longer have their mother on earth, remember that she is nevertheless closer than ever to her children. Remember also that there are duties to fulfill: to pray for her -especially the Holy Mass-, to visit her grave, to fulfill what was promised… * Those who still have her alive, remember your duties toward her: – to love her: not only in words, but in deeds, knowing how to show her that you love her! – to respect and honor her, before your own and before strangers. In the Sacred Scriptures we are warned: «Oh, how infamous is he who forsakes his father! And how accursed by God is he who exasperates his mother!» (Sir 3:18); «If one curses his father and his mother, his lamp will go out in deep darkness» (Prov 20:20); «The eyes that mock the father and do not look with respect on the mother, may the ravens of the brook pluck them out and the young eagles eat them!» (Prov 30:17). This severe language should not surprise us. Parents are God’s vicars for their children. -That is why parents must be obeyed «in the Lord» (Eph 6:1), and helped in their spiritual needs: company, conversation, prayers…, and also in their material needs: errands, household chores. On Mother’s Day all children give her a little gift. But always, every day, we must give her a great gift, the best of all: to study, to work, to behave well, to be obedient, responsible, to listen to her, in a word , to be good . This is what our mother wants from us! That is why the poet sang well of the mother, saying: A mother who is light is life itself! She is the only love that never ends, that within the heart, like an essence that purifies, flows out spreading. When grief casts down every belief this belief is never destroyed; and it stays clinging so to our souls that it seems the ivy of life. Everywhere, always the same, it comes with me, like a heavenly, unknown harmony; my heart has your name engraved upon it and so too does my imagination. It will be the last echo to sound on my dying lips, mother of mine! And in my tomb it will be a reliquary that will guard my gravestone and my shroud! 2 . Notes 1 [1] I follow in large part the beautiful book «The Mother» by the great Hungarian Cardinal Joseph Mindszenty. 2 [2] Guillermo Matta.
“On the wits and the energy of the unresigned will depend the course of the future”

Sermon preached by Fr. Carlos Miguel Buela on June 20, 1998, in the Parish of Our Lady of Sorrows, on the occasion of the clothing of the novices of the Institute of the Servants of the Lord and the Virgin of Matará We are celebrating the feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary. It is a particularly dear feast for us because our congregation began its public life on the day on which the Pope and all the bishops of the world consecrated the world −that is, all of us and all things− to the Immaculate Heart of Mary. That was on March 25, 1984. I always remember that here in San Rafael, on the day we were beginning with the diocesan seminary, the consecration was made by Bishop León Kruk in front of the parish of St. Joseph, whose pastor was Fr. Ortego, the youngest of all the priests of the diocese with his youthful 80 years. Mass was then celebrated on the sidewalk in front of his parish, and during the Mass the consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary was made. Just as She kept the things of her Son in her heart (cf. Lk 2:19), so we on this day, in remembering her, wish to keep her always in our heart. This week I was able to finish reading a book which is not recent, but is indeed very interesting, about St. James in Spain. In it I found a phrase that seemed to me very beautiful for the sermon of this day. The author says: “ On the wits and the energy of the unresigned will depend the course of the world ” 1 . It seems to me an appropriate occasion to develop what this means. I will begin with the final part of that phrase. “Will depend the course of the future” We men of our time forget −frequently, unfortunately− something that is very important: it is in our hands to be able to steer the course of the future. In the face of this, there are three differing positions: according to the Hebrews, works are enough; according to the Protestants, faith alone; the position of Catholics embraces both aspects: faith and works. The first position is the one held by the Jewish people by reason of their culture, their history and their way of seeing things. They are convinced that by acting, they bring about change. In fact they have shown it: nineteen hundred years after having lost their homeland, through tenacity, through acting, through working, they recovered it; another example is what happened with their language: the Hebrew language, which had been dead for nineteen hundred years, became −in what constitutes a unique case in the history of the world up to now− a living, spoken language; it is a language heard on radio and television; it is read in the newspapers and spoken by people in the streets. The other position is that of Protestantism. For them, as Luther said, faith alone is enough. It is with faith, without the need for works, that the future is changed. The Catholic position, which is neither the one nor the other, rises like a mountain above two valleys. Catholicism teaches: faith comes first, but works must accompany faith. That is to say, it is by reason of faith and by reason of works that the course of the future can −and must− be changed. Just as the Blessed Virgin did: she had faith, she believed in the Word she already bore in her Heart, she said “Yes” (cf. Lk 1:38) and began to bear her Word not only in her heart but also in her most holy womb, by accepting in faith and acting accordingly. She changed the course of the future! That woman who kept all the things of her Son (cf. Lk 2:29) is the greatest woman who has ever existed among all women. That is why her kinswoman Elizabeth greets her: Blessed are you among all women! (Lk 1:42). And as time goes on, the Blessed Virgin will be ever more exalted, as St. Louis Marie Grignion de Montfort says so well. And looking at that woman, seeking to imitate that woman who knew how to change the course of the future, we have had in this century a group of unresigned ones, who are the martyrs, the confessors of the faith, as were, for example, Cardinal Midzensty, Stépinac −who is about to be canonized 2 −; like the Chinese Cardinal Ignatius Kung Pin Mei; as John Paul II was and is. They did not resign themselves. They did not believe that nefarious political slogan −which was raised even within the ranks of the Church− that said: “better red than dead.” And they changed the course of history! The theorists spoke of the course of history inexorably marked out by ideology. It seemed something inevitable. And yet that group of unresigned ones changed the future. The course of history can be changed… We know that the course of history can be changed, first of all because we have faith, and because we know that God is the only one capable of moving the wills of men, and He moves them. In order to be able to change the future we must keep in mind when and where it is changed: that future is changed in the present, it is changed in the here and now; it is in the present that the future is changed. I always like to recall the triumph of General Wellington over Napoleon. Years after that resounding victory, he returned to the place where he had studied and, before all the cadets who admired him as a hero, he said these wise words: “Waterloo was won here.” In the classrooms where he studied and prepared himself. In the same way these young women will be able to say tomorrow that, like the Virgin, today they say their “Yes,” because it is a yes that springs from faith, and if it is accompanied by the works proper to faith it will certainly help to change the course of the future. “On the wits and the energy” The author names two elements: wits (or intelligence), and energy. Wits, that is, intelligence, that which distinguishes us men and women from irrational creatures. We are capable of thinking; animals do not think. But it is not enough merely to think; one must think and act. One must have energy of will, energy of character, in order to live in accordance with the truth the intellect knows. The future is changed precisely by the correct use of the two principal faculties of the soul: intellect and will. It is similar to what Solsyenitzin, one of the great men of this century, proposed. He spoke of “lucidity and courage.” To change the course of history it is necessary to have lucidity, that is, to have a lucid intellect capable of detecting problems and of finding adequate solutions; and one must have energy of will so as not to give in before those who would want other things. It is necessary to fight, and to fight is a grace. “Of the unresigned” Who are the unresigned ? They are those men and women who do not hand themselves over by placing themselves, improperly, in the hands of another. They are those who do not yield to public opinion when it is against the Gospel, because truth does not depend on the majority. When Pilate asks the majority: What do you want me to do with the one you call king of the Jews? (Mk 15:12), the majority shouted: Crucify him! Crucify him! (Mk 15:13). They are those who do not submit to the spirit of the world, because it is contrary to the Holy Spirit, to the Spirit of Truth, because the spirit of the world runs along other tracks, takes paths contrary to those of the Holy Spirit. I want to give some examples of what the ways of the world and its opinions are, and what the ways of the Holy Spirit are, which is the way of the unresigned : Today the majority fall into what has come to be called TV addiction; people live as slaves of television −called in Spain the idiot box . If one is not resigned, one asks oneself, “Why should I be a slave? I must be free.” By the grace of God, still up to now, we are not slaves of television; we do not habitually watch TV. Today many women live as slaves of the latest fashion craze; these Sisters of ours do not care at all about fashion; today they begin to wear a habit that will probably not change for years. That is to be unresigned . Today people live in a pansexualist culture; these Sisters are going to take a vow of chastity. Today people live preoccupied with money, they live as slaves of consumerism; these Sisters take a vow of poverty. Today people exalt freedom to the point of licentiousness; these Sisters will take a vow of obedience, which is not resignation, it is non-resignation , because it does not mean placing oneself in the hands of another human person, but is the gift of oneself, placing oneself totally in the hands of God, because it is wanting to do the will of God. It is exactly the opposite. We must form unresigned men and women We must seek to form unresigned men and women. We hear it said ad nauseam: “there are no vocations”; “young people today are busy with other things”; “in the past families were large and that is why there were many children who wanted to consecrate themselves, not now”; “priests are not needed”; “the place of the priest is taken by the laity…”. But if one is not resigned, one knows that God raises up vocations, that God does not let Himself be outdone in generosity by anyone, and that God sends vocations. And here we see it proven! “Many missionaries never went out from our country…”. And why should they not go out now? We must not resign ourselves! By the grace of God we have sent missionaries to the five continents, and by the grace of God I can repeat a phrase I have already used on another occasion: “ We are bleeding ourselves dry in missionaries .” It is also said: “Young people should not be asked for much sacrifice”; we propose sacrifice to them. “No, young people will be driven away by the cross of Christ…”. And it is the cross of Christ that calls young people! It is exactly the other way around! “High goals drive young people away…”; and it is high goals that call young people: we have young men studying extremely difficult languages: Chinese, Arabic, Russian, Quechua; the languages of tribes: the Chipibos, the Kachipos… “Young people do not know how to have fun…”. We have fun. “The sense of feast has been lost…”. Let us reconquer the sense of feast. The most famous phrase of the Constitutions is one of St. Athanasius: “From feast to feast we go toward the great Feast” 3 (It is the one the seminarians like most…!). That is fine; “from feast to feast” is our pilgrimage to the “great Feast” of Heaven. This position is not arbitrary, and it has a deep foundation: we are rebels against the world because we follow Jesus Christ, and that is why we are a sign of contradiction! We do not want young people who have crashed into the stars, but young people with a star, who know where to go, who follow the star! Not young people with a saddle, but young people with spurs, who are capable of having lucidity and courage! We aim to form men and women who are free with the freedom of the children of God! It is possible to change the course of history It is possible to change the course of history, but only with unresigned men and women, who freely follow the way of the Holy Spirit, which is the way that will lead them to bear witness to God before those who do not know Him. If these Sisters accompany today’s “yes” with works, they will certainly contribute to changing the course of history, and the history of many souls. On how many of these Sisters so many souls in so many places will depend! How great is the good they are called to do, how important is the courageous witness of regarding God as an Absolute in their lives! How many men and women will feel edified by the witness of these Sisters! We want men and women capable of changing the course of history!
