1950th Anniversary of the Martyrdom of Sts. Peter and Paul

Watch the video on YouTube ↗ 1950 years ago, the land of Rome, founded by Romulus and Remus, would witness the passage of two new founders, the apostle of the key and the apostle of the sword, who, following the command of their Master with their total witness, would become the pillars of the City of God among men. St. Peter, on the one hand, was the Fisherman to whom our Lord said, ‘Do not be afraid; from now on you will be a fisher of men’ (cf. Lk 5:5-6, 10) St. Peter was the Witness who was present at the Transfiguration of the Lord, at His Agony in the Garden, and at His Resurrection. St. Peter was the Preacher of True Freedom, who taught in his letter: “Act as men who are truly free, obeying God, and not as those who make freedom an excuse for their malice” (1 Pet 2:16) St. Peter was the Wonderworker to whom multitudes flocked so that, as he passed by, at least his shadow might fall on some of them, and all were healed. (cf. Acts 5:14-16). St. Peter was, finally, the Pope , the Vicar of Christ on earth, because Christ Himself said: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church (Mt 16:18). St. Paul, for his part, was the Apostle of the Gentiles who m ost gladly spent himself and was spent for souls. (cf. 2 Cor 12:15). St. Paul was the Tireless Traveler , making three missionary journeys and five visits to Jerusalem. St. Paul was the Persecuted One , teaching that we are “persecuted , but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed (2 Cor 4:7) . St. Paul was the Formator who instructed the Romans, saying: “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind” (Rom 12:2) St. Paul was, finally, the Missionary who taught with his life that “ The love of Christ urges us on” (2 Cor 5:14) On a day like today, both gave Christ the supreme witness of love: St. Peter shedding his blood as he died crucified head downward, and St. Paul dying by beheading. St. Augustine would say: “Merit made their passion equal, and charity made it fall on the same day. Thus did He accomplish it in them who was in them, and who suffered in them and with them, who helps those who fight and crowns the victors” 1 That is why even today, after 1950 years, it is our ideal to be faithful to their glorious legacy. Because to love the Incarnate Word is to love His Successor and His Church, “founded on the Apostles and perpetuated by apostolic succession” 2 , “our motto” being “‘with Peter and under Peter’” 3 . Because we are convinced that: “Where Peter is, there is the Church” 4 , and with loving impetus, like Peter, we have left everything 5 and must go throughout the world proclaiming with him: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God (Mt 16:16) and there is no other name under heaven by which we can be saved (Acts 4:10) 6 . Because we seek to be formed with a Roman spirit, the spirit of the Eternal City of the Apostles Peter and Paul, which “means being witnesses, day by day, to the living tradition of the faith, as it is proclaimed by the See of Peter” 7 Because, in imitation of the Apostles who, obedient to Christ’s command, Go and teach all all nations…, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you , it is our desire to undertake with joy and courage the missionary adventure, announcing to all men that Jesus Christ has become for you, from God, wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption (1 Cor 1:30) 8 . And we wish to make our own the Apostle’s cry: Woe to me if I do not preach the Gospel! (1 Cor 9:16). Because that is what the Apostles did, according to the words of St. Paul to the Corinthians: “all our missionary and apostolic work is founded on the conviction that He must reign (1 Cor 15:25)” 9 . That is why “we do not want ‘to leave anything untried so that the love of Christ may have the supreme primacy in the Church and in society’” 10 . Because today the words of the Apostle of the Gentiles, God wills all men to be saved and to come to the full knowledge of the Truth (1 Tim 2:4), continue to be for us the rule and foundation of all our missionary activity 11 Because, inspired by the great Formator of Apostles that St. Paul was, we want “to imitate Jesus Christ as perfectly as possible; we want to strive fervently and resolutely to have the same mind that was in Christ Jesus… (Phil 2:5), so that we may be the aroma of Christ (2 Cor 2:15), ambassadors of Christ (2 Cor 5:20) … of the mystery of the Gospel (Eph 6:19), a letter of Christ (2 Cor 3:3), clothed with Christ (Gal 3:27), firmly convinced that we are predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son (Rom 8:29), becoming like Him (cf. Phil 3:10), and being configured to Him (cf. Phil 3:10). […]Until we can say, in all truth, with the Apostle, Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ (1 Cor 11:1), and it is no longer I who live, it is Christ who lives in me (Gal 2:20)” 12 . Because today, just as in apostolic times, our missionaries on the five continents must repeat with Peter to so many others: Silver and gold I have none; but what I have, I give you , and, in the name of Jesus Christ, devote themselves eagerly to the works of mercy. Because today, following the counsel of St. Paul, Persevere always in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving (Col 4:2) , our monks, with their sacrifices and prayers, must be “magnets of the grace of God” 13 . Because today, 1950 years after Peter and Paul gave their supreme witness of belonging to Christ by the shedding of their blood, we too must be ready, out of loyalty to God, for martyrdom 14 , and with the same Apostle we must say: for me to live is Christ and to die is gain (Phil 1:21) 15 . Because today, from East and West, on the five continents, we religious of the Incarnate Word desire to keep marching on rejoicing in hope (Rom 12:12) 16 and with intrepid ardor we say: Possumus! since we know in whom we have put our trust (cf. 2 Tim 1:12) 17 , and with the Apostle we exclaim: I can do all things in Him who strengthens me (Phil 4:13). That is why we must advance without fear, with the firm conviction that all things work together for the good of those who love God (Rom 8:28). Because the passion of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul has made this day sacred for us. Following their examples: “Let us love their faith, their life, their labors, their sufferings, their confession and preaching of the faith. Let us make our way pass before the gaze of the Lord. A way that was narrow, steep and full of brambles, but the passage of so many others has made it smooth. For the Lord Himself was the first to pass along it; the intrepid apostles also passed along it… and with them He who said: Without me you can do nothing . (Cf. St. Augustine, Sermon 295, 8) To the Queen of Apostles we entrust ourselves, so that She may make of us: “true apostles to whom the Lord of hosts will give the word and the strength needed to work wonders and to win glorious spoils from His enemies. Apostles who have the silvered wings of the dove, to fly, with the pure intention of the glory of God and the salvation of men, wherever the Holy Spirit calls us. Apostles who leave behind them, in the places where they preach, only the gold of charity, which is the fulfillment of the whole law (cf. Rom 13:10). Apostles who carry in their mouths the two-edged sword of the word of God (Heb 4:12); on their shoulders, the blood-stained standard of the cross; in their right hand, the crucifix; the rosary in their left; the sacred names of Jesus and Mary in their hearts, and in all their conduct the modesty and mortification of Jesus Christ” 18 . Apostles, in short, who may, by the power of divine grace, imitate and carry out in their lives the glorious example and indelible teaching of the Holy Apostles, Patrons of Rome Sts. Peter and Paul, pray for us and for the whole world. Notes 1 St. Augustine, Sermon 299A 2 Constitutions, 279 . 3 Constitutions, 211 . 4 Directory of the Eastern Branch , 103; op. cit. Eucharistic Profession of Faith

Download PDF Eucharistic Profession of Faith Public manifestation of faith in the august sacrament of the altar Feast of Corpus Christi, 1992 Dear Brothers: On this Solemnity of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ we wish to manifest, as a community and publicly, the faith of the Catholic, Apostolic and Roman Church concerning the august sacrament of the altar. Institution 1. How do you know that the Eucharist is a sacrament? Because the Magisterium of the Church / solemnly declares it so in her Councils. 2. In which Councils? In that of Florence: / “The third is the sacrament of the Eucharist, / the matter of which is wheat bread / and wine of the grape…” (Dz 698); / and, moreover, among others, / the Council of Trent: / “If anyone says / that the sacraments of the New Law… / are more or fewer than seven, / namely: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist /…, let him be anathema” (Dz 844). 3. Who instituted the sacrament of the Eucharist directly, and where? Our Lord Jesus Christ instituted it at the Last Supper; / the Council of Trent declares: / “All our forefathers /…expressly professed that our Redeemer / instituted this so wonderful sacrament at the Last Supper” (Dz 874) 4. What are the sources in which the Church finds this doctrine? These sources are three: / first, the three Synoptic Gospels; / second, the Gospel of St. John; / and third, the Apostle St. Paul. 5. What do the Synoptic Gospels teach? St. Matthew (26:26-29), / St. Mark (14:22-25) / and St. Luke (22:15-20) / unanimously teach three things: / – First, that Jesus Christ instituted the Most Holy Eucharist / by giving his body and his blood as food and drink, / thus replacing the meal of the paschal lamb. / – Second, that he commanded his supper to be repeated : / “Do this in memory of me” / – Third, that he commanded that the Eucharist be eaten and drunk : / “… eat … this is my Body ; … drink … this is my Blood ” 6. What does St. John (6:55-59) remind us of? He reminds us of the teaching of Jesus: / – First. That the celebration of the Eucharist is to be repeated, / because no one will have life / without eating the Body of Christ and drinking his Blood; / – Second. That by the institution of Christ / it remains at the disposal of men / so that all might partake of his life-giving Flesh. 7. In what words does Jesus say this? “I am the living Bread come down from Heaven / Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood / has eternal life / … for my flesh is true food / and my blood true drink /… whoever eats my flesh will live because of me /… whoever eats this bread will live forever”. 8. Does this also teach that the Eucharist gives us sanctifying grace? Of course. / The union and abiding of man in Christ / and of Christ in man, / the participation and communion between man and Christ, / and eternal life, / cannot be obtained without sanctifying grace. 9. What does St. Paul teach? (1 Cor 11:20-25) First of all, the Apostle St. Paul declares / the historical truth of the institution, by our Lord, / of the Holy Eucharist, / presenting it as a banquet, / as the real presence of Christ, / as a sacrifice, and as perpetuated until his Second Coming / by means of his ministers. Essence 10. What is the matter of the Eucharist? The proper matter of the Eucharist / is wheat bread and wine of the grape. 11. What is the form of this sacrament? The proper form of the consecration of this sacrament / is the words of Christ: / “This is my Body” / and “This is my Blood” / (or “This is the chalice of my Blood”). 12. Why is it the proper and fitting form of the sacrament? It is the proper and fitting form / because it signifies what is done in the sacrament, / since the words declare the conversion of the bread into the true Body of Christ / and of the wine into his Blood. 13. How does the celebrating priest utter the words of consecration? The celebrating priest utters the words of the Consecration in two ways and simultaneously: / – First, recitatively, narrating the historical event of the Supper: / “Who (Christ), on the eve of his Passion…”; / – Second, and principally, assertively, / affirming the words spoken by Christ as his own, / that is, speaking “in Persona Christi,” / with those words bearing upon the matter that the priest has present on the altar. Real presence 14. How is our Lord Jesus Christ present in the sacrament of the altar? Our Lord Jesus Christ is truly, / really / and substantially present / in the Most Blessed Sacrament of the altar. 15. What does truly mean? Truly means that his presence is not merely in figure, / as Zwingli held, / but in truth. 16. What does really mean? Really means that his presence is not mere subjective faith, / as Oecolampadius held, / but in reality. 17. What does substantially mean? Substantially means that the presence of the Lord in the Eucharist is not merely virtual, / as Calvin held, / but substantial. 18. What does the Council of Trent teach on this as a defined dogma of faith? The Council of Trent teaches: / “If anyone denies / that in the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist / there are contained truly, / really, / and substantially / the body and blood / together with the soul and divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ, / and therefore the whole Christ; / but says that he is in it only as in a sign and figure / or by his power, / let him be anathema”. (Dz. 883) 19. With what body and with what blood is Jesus Christ present in the Eucharist? Our Lord Jesus Christ is present in the Eucharist / with the same body and blood that was born of the Virgin Mary, / the same body that hung upon the cross / and the same blood that flowed from his side. On Transubstantiation 20. What is the conversion of the bread and wine that occurs at the moment of the Consecration called? This wonderful and singular conversion is properly called “Transubstantiation,” / not consubstantiation, as Luther held. 21. Why is it called wonderful? It is called wonderful / because it is a most lofty mystery, / beyond the capacity of every created intellect. / It is the Mystery of faith! 22. Why is it called singular? It is called singular / because in all creation there exists / no conversion like this one. 23. What happens in transubstantiation? In transubstantiation the whole substance of the bread and the whole substance of the wine disappear / as they are converted into the Body, Blood, Soul and Divinity of Christ. 24. In such a way? In such a way that under each of the species / and under every part of the species, / before separation and after separation, / the whole Christ is contained. 25. It is of faith, therefore, that the whole and only substance of the bread and wine is transubstantiated into the whole and only substance of the body and blood of Christ. Now then, what is it that remains? What remain in the Eucharist, without a subject of inherence, by the power of God, / are the accidents, species or appearances of bread and wine. 26. What are they? The accidents that remain after transubstantiation are: / the weight, size, taste, quantity, smell, color, flavor, shape, measure, etc., / of bread and of wine. / Only the substance changes. 27. What is contained under the species of bread by virtue of the words? By virtue of the words, / under the species of bread is contained / the body of Christ. 28. And by virtue of accompaniment or concomitance? Together with the body, / by natural connection, / are contained the blood and the soul, and, / by the wonderful hypostatic union, / the divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ. 29. What is contained under the species of wine by virtue of the words? By virtue of the words / the blood of Christ is contained / under the species of wine. 30. And by virtue of concomitance? Together with the blood, / by natural connection, / are contained the body, the soul and, / by the hypostatic union, / the divinity of Christ. On the Sacrifice 31. Is the Mass a true and proper sacrifice? The Council of Trent teaches as a defined truth of faith: / “If anyone says that in the sacrifice of the Mass / a true and proper sacrifice is not offered to God, / or that to offer it is nothing other than Christ being given to us to eat, / let him be anathema”. (Dz. 948) 32. Did God foretell the Eucharistic sacrifice? Yes, / already in the Old Testament God foretold / the sacrifice of the Mass by figures and prophecies: / through the prophet Malachi (1:10-11), / through the sacrifice of Melchizedek (Gen 14:18 ff.), / and through the sacrifice of the Paschal Lamb (Ex 12:3 ff.). 33. When did he teach that the Mass is a sacrifice? He taught that the Mass is a sacrifice / when he instituted it: / “… this is my body which will be given up …” (Lk 22:19); / “… this is my blood… which will be poured out …” (Mt 26:28; Mk 14:24; Lk 22:20). / To give up his body and pour out his blood for us / for the forgiveness of sins / shows that he offers himself in sacrifice. 34. When does he command that the Eucharistic sacrifice be perpetuated? He commands that the Eucharistic sacrifice be perpetuated / when he adds: / “Do this in memory of me” (Lk 22:19; 1 Cor 11:24‑25) / and the Apostle further adds: / “Each time you eat this bread and drink this cup, / you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes” (1 Cor 11:26). / This proclamation or living representation / is in fact / carried out in every Mass, / thus perpetuating the sacrifice of the Cross. Essence of the Eucharistic sacrifice 35. What does the Mass represent and what does it commemorate? The sacrifice of the Mass is representative / and commemorative of the sacrifice of the Cross. / Therefore: “As often as the memorial of this sacrifice is celebrated, / the work of our Redemption is renewed”. (Prayer of the assembly of the 2nd Sunday in Ordinary Time). 36. What does representative mean? Representative means that it makes present again the sacrifice of the Cross. / It is not an empty and lifeless representation, / nor a subjective recollection, / but an objective commemoration / and a living and full representation, / true and wonderful, / containing Christ, the Victim of the Passion, / and the separated species of bread and wine / representing the Passion itself, / through the mystical separation of the body and the blood. 37. What does the Church teach in her solemn magisterium? The Council of Trent teaches: / “If anyone says / that the sacrifice of the Mass is only one of praise and thanksgiving, / or a mere commemoration of the sacrifice accomplished on the Cross, / but not propitiatory; / or that it benefits only the one who receives; / and that it ought not to be offered for the living and the dead, / for sins, punishments, satisfactions and other necessities, / let him be anathema”. (Dz. 950) 38. Is Holy Mass a sacrifice only by its relation to the sacrifice of the Cross? The sacrifice of the Mass is not only an objective, / living and express representation of the sacrifice of the Cross; / it is not constituted solely by this relation / —which is essential to it— / but this relation is so essential to it / that Christ the Priest, by an unbloody immolation, / does on the altar what he did once and for all on the Cross, / offering himself to God the Father / as Victim for the salvation of all men. 39. Are the sacrifice of the Cross and the sacrifice of the Mass distinct? No. / The sacrifice of the Cross and the sacrifice of the Mass are one and the same, / because the Victim is one and the same, / the Priest is one and the same, / and the oblative act is one and the same. 40. Do they differ in anything? Yes. / They differ in something accidental: / -First, on the part of the Victim: / on the cross the sacrifice was bloody; / in the Mass the sacrifice is unbloody; / -Second, on the part of the Priest: / on the Cross Christ offered himself alone and visibly; / in the Mass he offers himself invisibly, through the hands of priests; / -Third, on the part of the effect: / on the Cross he made satisfaction and merited superabundantly for all men of all times; / in the Mass the merits / and the satisfaction for sins accomplished on the Cross are applied to new generations. 41. What is the thing offered in the Mass? The Victim offered in the Mass / is the body and blood of Christ as poured out in the Passion. / In other words: / it is the same suffering Christ, the Christ who has suffered. 42. Is the thing offered only the suffering Christ? Not only is the suffering Christ offered, / but with him all his members are offered, / the whole Church, the Mystical Body of Christ. 43. What is required for the sacrifice to have its full effect? For the sacrifice to have its full effect / it is necessary that the faithful immolate themselves as victims; / that is why the celebrant asks: / “May he make of us an eternal offering” (Euch. Prayer III), / or “that we may become in Christ a living sacrifice in praise of your glory” (Euch. Prayer IV). 44. What is the essence of the sacrifice of the Mass? The essence of the sacrifice of the Mass / is found at the moment of the double consecration of the species, / ordered to communion / as an integral part. 45. Why is the essence of the Mass found in the separate consecration of the species of bread and wine alone? Because there is found the true representation of the sacrifice of the cross, / in the separation of the two species, / under which the body and blood of Christ are present / by virtue of the words of consecration, / a mystical or sacramental immolation being carried out, / wonderfully suited to represent Christ immolated, that is, / with his body and his blood separated, / as they were on the Cross. 46. Why does the consecration bring about the sacrifice? The Eucharistic consecration brings about the sacrifice for two reasons: / First, it is the unbloody, mystical or sacramental immolation of Christ / under the separated species of bread and wine, / which represent and perpetuate in an unbloody manner the bloody immolation of the Cross; / and second, it is at the same time a ritual oblation / made by Jesus Christ, the principal Priest, / through the hands of the visible priests, / in honor of the majesty of God. On the ministers 47. Who is the principal offerer of the sacrifice of the Mass? The principal Priest of the sacrifice of the Mass is Jesus Christ, / our Lord, / as is seen from the very words of the consecration, / in which the visible priest makes present the body and blood of Christ in the name of Christ: / “This is my body… This is my blood,” / acting ‘in Persona Christi’. 48. How is he the principal Priest? Jesus Christ is the Principal Priest of Holy Mass / inasmuch as with an actual will / he wills and offers each and every Mass / celebrated on earth. 49. How does he offer them? Jesus Christ as principal Priest / offers each and every transubstantiation by a single interior oblative act, / without innovation or succession, / not by successive acts of oblation. / This oblation, which continues without interruption, / is the same interior oblation of the sacrifice of the Cross, / though not gaining new merit, / but applying the merits gained on the Cross. 50. Who are the ministers of the Eucharistic sacrifice? All validly ordained priests, and they alone, / are ministers of the sacrifice of the Mass. 51. Furthermore, does the whole Church offer the Mass? Yes, the Church, comprising all the faithful who make it up, / offers each Eucharistic sacrifice. 52. How do the faithful offer the sacrifice of the Mass? The faithful participate, not in the consecration, but in the oblation. / They participate in it, without performing the visible liturgical rite, in two ways: – First, by offering the Victim through the hands of the priest, / who was publicly chosen by the bishop to offer the sacrifice in the name of all of them; / – Second, by offering the Victim together with the priest, / in such a way that in the very oblation of the Victim / —made by Christ and by the visible priest— / they offer themselves to God the Father / as “living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God” (Rom 12:1), / offering also their own spiritual sacrifices, their concerns, their sorrows, anguish, miseries and needs, / uniting their prayers or desires of praise, petition, expiation and thanksgiving / to the intention of the priest and of Christ himself, the principal Priest, / so that they may be offered to God the Father in the same oblation of the Victim. 53. When does the offering of the faithful begin? The offering of the faithful begins with the procession of the offerings for the presentation of the gifts of bread and wine, / reaches its fullness when the priest places the Victim upon the altar, / is sustained throughout the memorial oblation / and is solemnly affirmed with the “Amen” of the final doxology. On the sacrificial Banquet 54. What is the most perfect participation in Holy Mass? The most perfect participation in the Mass / “…consists in the faithful receiving the body of the Lord from the same sacrifice” (Vat. II, S.C., 55). 55. What conditions are indicated for receiving the sacrament of the Eucharist fruitfully? For receiving the sacrament of the Eucharist fruitfully / three things are indicated: / To be in the grace of God, without awareness of mortal sin; / To have fasted for one hour beforehand; / To know Whom one is going to receive and to approach Communion with devotion. 56. What images does the Second Vatican Council use to impress upon us the importance of the Mass? The Council says that it is summit and source: / “it is the summit toward which the activity of the whole Church is directed and, / at the same time, / the source from which all her power flows” (Vat. II, S. C., 10) Dear brothers: Come! Let us adore so great a sacrament! Let us participate ever more actively, more consciously and more fruitfully in the one true sacrifice for the salvation of all men! Contents Institution. 1 Essence 4 Real presence 5 On Transubstantiation. 6 On the Sacrifice. 8 Essence of the Eucharistic sacrifice. 9 On the ministers 13 On the sacrificial Banquet 15
Placing and blessing of the IVE Cross on the Hill of Crosses in Lithuania

Cross in Lithuania “And I, once lifted up from the earth, will draw all to Myself” (Jn 12:32) After Mass we go in procession with hymns to the place where the Cross of the IVE is planted on the Hill of Crosses. On arriving in front of the cross, the celebrant says: [We have gathered here, on the Hill of Crosses, a mystical place of Christendom in Lithuania, to proclaim to the world that] The Cross of our Lord —the means chosen by infinite wisdom “to give life to many and in this way to transfigure the world” 1 — is also for us what it was for Christ: “the greatest proof of love” 2 . For the Cross “was the chair from which [the Incarnate Word] taught, the altar on which he was immolated, the temple of his prayer, the arena where he fought, and as it were the forge from which so many wonders came forth” 3 . And therefore, from the beginnings of our beloved Institute, the Cross that the Incarnate Word chose for Himself has been the noble emblem that identifies us and the solemn proclamation that, for our members, the exceedingly great and sacred task of the evangelization of culture is a cross; and that the cross is our program and the royal road we have chosen in order to follow the Incarnate Word “amid the persecutions that are never lacking to the Church” 4 , and that it is in this very cross that we find all joy and all hope fulfilled on this earth. That is why this Cross, which today we are to plant in this soil, is an image of the perennial and fervent desire that our little Religious Family be “never folded in upon itself, but open like the arms of Christ on the Cross, whose arms were dislocated from opening them so wide in love” 5 , so that its present and future members, “taking up their cross [courageously] and sharing in the sufferings of Christ” 6 , may cooperate in “the most divine of divine works” 7 , which is the eternal salvation of souls, and that in this way our world may be transfigured. May this Cross, which bears at its center the coat of arms of our Institute, be a sign of our commitment to bear witness before the world that in the Cross of Christ is found all Truth and the very Wisdom that must be preached. May our Religious Family, in the shadow of this Cross —which “is the mighty weapon of Christ, the staff of the Good Shepherd, with which the divine David goes out to fight the infernal Goliath and with which he knocks with authority at the door of heaven and it is opened to him” 8 — find all its strength in weakness, all its riches in its most austere poverty, and the most consoling joy in the midst of arduous trials. “O triumphant Cross of Christ, inspire us to continue the task of evangelization! O glorious Cross of Christ, strengthen us to proclaim and to live the Gospel of salvation! O victorious Cross of Christ, our only hope, lead us to the joy and peace of the Resurrection and eternal life!” 9 Prayer of blessing When the homily is over, the celebrant, standing before the cross with hands extended, says the prayer of blessing (which may be preceded by a hymn): We bless you, Lord, holy Father, who in the excess of your love obtained for us the remedy of salvation and of life on the tree from which the first man had drawn ruin and death. For when the hour of his Passover came, Jesus the Lord, priest, teacher and king, freely ascended the tree of the cross and made it the throne of his glory, the altar of his sacrifice, the chair of truth. There, lifted up above the earth, he conquered the ancient enemy and, clothed in the purple of his blood, drew all men to himself, full of love; there, with arms outstretched, he made to you, Father, the offering of his life and poured saving power into the sacraments of the New Covenant; there he taught by his death what he had earlier announced by word: that the grain of wheat, when it dies, bears abundant fruit. Therefore we beseech you, Lord, that your faithful, in venerating this sign of salvation, may receive the fruits of redemption that Christ Jesus merited by his Passion; that on the cross they may put their sins to death and that, by the power of this cross, they may overcome pride and strengthen their weakness; that in it they may find consolation in their afflictions and security in their dangers; and that, protected by its power, they may travel unharmed along the roads of this world, until you, Father, receive them into the heavenly Homeland. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. R. Amen. The cross is then sprinkled with holy water and incensed while a hymn is sung. X Prayer after the blessing of the Cross : E ternal Father, Lord of history, who in your designs of infinite mercy willed that your Son become man to redeem man by his death on the Cross. I ncarnate Word, “who died and rose again, who suffered misunderstanding, persecution and condemnation at the hands of the powerful; who, after passing among us doing good to all by word and deed, healing the sick and feeding the hungry, allowed yourself to be nailed to the Cross” 10 . H oly Spirit, who strengthen with every virtue 11 the followers of the Crucified according to the might of his glory, for all patience and long-suffering with joy 12 . O Most Holy Trinity, receive this Cross which today rises up to your throne imploring the grace of “the folly of the cross , which makes one wiser than the wisdom of all men” 13 for all the members, present and future, of the Religious Family of the Incarnate Word. I ncarnate Word, to whom God the Father granted the Name above every name , and in whose Name we are gathered, grant us perseverance to the end in the honorable office of serving you “even in the most difficult situations and in the most adverse conditions” 14 . C hrist Crucified, who said when I am lifted up from the earth I will draw all to Myself 15 , grant us the grace that, through the witness and preaching of your Triumph on the Cross, “men and women, and particularly the young, may be supernaturally drawn to follow your way of life solely by the glory of the Cross, the wisdom and power of God” 16 . S weet Christ Crucified, grant your missionaries to fight with confidence in the power of your cross and to raise aloft throughout the whole world the precious standard of your Cross. M ay the light of your cross, O Lord, illumine and give meaning to all our crosses. T his we implore of you, we your children of the Religious Family of the Incarnate Word, through the loving intercession of your Mother and our Mother, the steadfast Witness at the foot of your Cross. T oday and always, Lord, may the Triumph of the Cross be our triumph. Amen. Final blessing of the Celebration Notes 1 Directory of Evangelization of Culture , 164; op. cit. Cf. Dialogue for the 2nd Youth Day

Dialogue for the 1st Day of Families in San Rafael San Rafael, 1997 Part I Dear brothers and sisters: In this procession we wish to hold a dialogue on the rights of the family , for, as the motto of this Day convoked by His Holiness John Paul II states, the family is a gift and a hope-filled commitment for humanity. Therefore, in order to become aware of the challenges facing the Family in the Third Millennium, we wish to follow the text of the “Charter of the Rights of the Family” presented by the Holy See, the central and supreme governing body of the Catholic Church, to all persons, institutions and authorities concerned with the mission of the family in the contemporary world. The Bishops gathered in Synod in Rome in 1980 asked for this charter. Pope John Paul II confirmed this request 1 to present a formulation –as complete and orderly as possible– of the fundamental rights of that natural and universal society which is the family. These rights ultimately derive from the law inscribed by the Creator in the heart of every human being. All the Episcopal Conferences of the world and the leading experts in the field were consulted. Thus, respect for these rights must be promoted and their effective recognition and observance ensured. Preamble of the Charter . The Preamble of the Charter sets out the foundations of the rights of the family. Do the rights of the human person have a social dimension? The rights of the person, even though expressed as rights of the individual, have a fundamentally social dimension which finds an innate and vital expression in the family 2 . Is the family founded on marriage? The family is founded on marriage, that intimate union of life, a complement between a man and a woman, which is constituted by the indissoluble bond of marriage, freely contracted, publicly affirmed, and which is open to the transmission of life 3 . What is the only institution that transmits life? Marriage is the natural institution to which the mission of transmitting life is exclusively entrusted 4 . Does the family exist before the State? The family, a natural society, exists prior to the State or any other community, and possesses inherent rights which are inalienable 5 . What is most important about the family? The family constitutes, much more than a mere juridical, social and economic unit, a community of love and solidarity, which is irreplaceable for the teaching and transmission of the cultural, ethical, social, spiritual and religious values essential for the development and well-being of its own members and of society 6 . Is the family a place of encounter and of help? The family is the place where different generations come together and help one another to grow in human wisdom and to harmonize individual rights with the other demands of social life 7 . Do the family and society complement each other? The family and society, which are mutually linked by vital and organic bonds, have a complementary function in the defense and promotion of the good of humanity and of every person 8 . Must society defend the family? The experience of different cultures throughout history has shown the need for society to recognize and defend the institution of the family 9 . How must society help the family? Society, and in a particular manner the State and International Organizations, must protect the family through measures of a political, economic, social and juridical character, which aim at consolidating the unity and stability of the family so that it can exercise its specific function 10 . Is the family under attack? The rights, the fundamental needs, the well-being and the values of the family, even though they are progressively being safeguarded in many cases, are often ignored and not rarely undermined by laws, institutions and socio-economic programs 11 . Does poverty threaten the dignity of the family? Many families are forced to live in situations of poverty which prevent them from carrying out their own mission with dignity 12 . Why does the Church defend the family? The Catholic Church, aware that the good of the person, of society and of the Church herself passes by way of the family, has always held it part of her mission to proclaim to all the plan of God intrinsic to human nature concerning marriage and the family, to promote these two institutions and to defend them against every attack directed against them 13 . Part II Article 1 Are all persons free to choose their state of life? All persons have the right to the free choice of their state of life and thus the right to marry and establish a family or to remain single 14 . a) Is there a right to marry and establish a family? Every man and every woman, having reached marriageable age and having the necessary capacity, has the right to marry and establish a family without any discrimination whatsoever; legal restrictions on the exercise of this right, whether permanent or temporary in nature, can be introduced only when they are required by grave and objective demands of the institution of marriage itself and of its social and public character; they must respect in all cases the dignity and the fundamental rights of the person 15 . b) What conditions must society provide? All those who wish to marry and establish a family have the right to expect from society the moral, educational, social and economic conditions which will enable them to exercise their right to marry in all maturity and responsibility 16 . c) Must public authorities recognize the institutional value of marriage? The institutional value of marriage must be recognized by the public authorities; the situation of unmarried couples must not be placed on the same level as marriage duly contracted 17 . Article 2 Is free and full consent necessary for marriage? Marriage cannot be contracted except by the free and full consent of the spouses duly expressed 18 . a) Must families avoid exerting undue pressure on the choice? With due respect for the traditional role of the families in certain cultures in guiding the decision of their children, all pressure which would impede the choice of a specific person as spouse is to be avoided 19 . b) Must the religious freedom of the spouses be respected? The future spouses have the right to have their religious liberty respected. Therefore, to impose as a prior condition for marriage a denial of faith or a profession of faith which is contrary to conscience constitutes a violation of this right 20 . c) Do man and woman have the same dignity and equal rights? The spouses, in the natural complementarity which exists between man and woman, enjoy the same dignity and equal rights regarding marriage 21 . Part III Article 3 Do the spouses have the right to decide responsibly on the number of children to have? The spouses have the inalienable right to found a family and to decide on the spacing of births and the number of children to be born, taking into full consideration their duties towards themselves, their children already born, the family and society, in a just hierarchy of values and in accordance with the objective moral order which excludes recourse to contraception, sterilization and abortion 22 . a) Is interference by public authority regarding the number of children to have a grave offense against human dignity and justice? The activities of public authorities or private organizations which attempt in any way to limit the freedom of couples in deciding about their children constitute a grave offense against human dignity and justice 23 . b) Is it licit to make economic aid conditional on limiting the number of children? In international relations, economic aid for the advancement of peoples must not be conditioned on acceptance of programs of contraception, sterilization or abortion 24 . c) Does the family have the right to be helped by society? The family has a right to assistance by society in the bearing and rearing of children. Married couples with large families have a right to adequate aid and should not be subjected to discrimination 25 . Article 4 From what moment must human life be respected? Human life must be respected and protected absolutely from the moment of conception 26 . a) Does abortion violate human rights? Abortion is a direct violation of the fundamental right to life of the human being 27 . b) Is it licit to manipulate the human embryo? Respect for the dignity of the human being excludes all experimental manipulation or exploitation of the human embryo 28 . c) Is any intervention on a person's genetic heritage licit? All interventions on the genetic heritage of the human person that are not aimed at correcting anomalies constitute a violation of the right to bodily integrity and contradict the good of the family. d) Do children have rights? Children, both before and after birth, have the right to special protection and assistance, as do their mothers during pregnancy and for a reasonable period of time after childbirth 29 . e) Do all children have equal rights? All children, whether born in or out of wedlock, enjoy the same right to social protection with a view to their integral personal development 30 . f) Must orphans have special protection from society? Orphans and children who are deprived of the assistance of their parents or guardians must receive special protection on the part of society. With regard to foster care or adoption, the State must provide legislation which assists suitable families to welcome into their homes children who are in need of temporary or permanent care and which at the same time respects the natural rights of the parents 31 . g) And children with disabilities? Handicapped children have the right to find in the home and the school an environment suitable to their human development 32 . Part IV Article 5 Do parents have the right to educate their children? Since they have conferred life on their children, parents have the original, primary and inalienable right to educate them; hence they must be acknowledged as the first and foremost educators of their children 33 . a) Must they educate them according to their convictions? Parents have the right to educate their children in conformity with their moral and religious convictions, taking into account the cultural traditions of the family which favor the good and the dignity of the child; they should also receive from society the necessary aid and assistance to perform their educational role properly 34 . b) Do parents have the right to choose the schools for their children? Parents have the right to choose freely schools or other means necessary to educate their children in keeping with their convictions. Public authorities must ensure that public subsidies are allocated in such a way that parents are truly free to exercise this right without incurring unjust burdens. Parents should not have to sustain, directly or indirectly, extra charges which would deny or unjustly limit the exercise of this freedom 35 . c) Do they have the right that their children not be compelled to attend classes they do not agree with? Parents have the right to ensure that their children are not compelled to attend classes which are not in agreement with their own moral and religious convictions. In particular, sex education –which is a basic right of the parents– must always be carried out under their close supervision, whether at home or in educational centers chosen and controlled by them 36 . d) Is it licit for the State to impose a compulsory system of education that excludes all religious formation? The rights of parents are violated when a compulsory system of education is imposed by the State from which all religious formation is excluded 37 . e) Must parents take part in the educational work of schools? The primary right of parents to educate their children must be upheld in all forms of collaboration between parents, teachers and school authorities, and particularly in forms of participation designed to give citizens a voice in the functioning of schools and in the formulation and implementation of educational policies 38 . f) Does the family have the right to be helped, and not attacked, by the media? The family has the right to expect that the means of social communication will be positive instruments for the building up of society, and that they will reinforce the fundamental values of the family. At the same time the family has the right to be adequately protected, especially with regard to its youngest members, from the negative effects and misuse of the mass media 39 . Article 6 Does the family have the right to exist and to progress? The family has the right to exist and to progress as a family 40 . a) Must public authority respect families? Public authorities must respect and foster the dignity, lawful independence, privacy, integrity and stability of every family 41 . b) Does divorce threaten the family? Divorce attacks the very institution of marriage and of the family 42 . c) Must the extended family be held in esteem? The extended family system, where it exists, should be held in esteem and helped to carry out better its traditional role of solidarity and mutual assistance, while at the same time respecting the rights of the nuclear family and the personal dignity of each member. Part V Article 7 Does the family have the right to live its own religious life? Every family has the right to live freely its own domestic religious life under the guidance of the parents, as well as the right to profess publicly and to propagate the faith, to take part in public worship and in freely chosen programs of religious instruction, without suffering any discrimination 43 . Article 8 Does the family have a right in the building up of society? The family has the right to exercise its social and political function in the construction of society 44 . a) Do families have the right to form associations? Families have the right to form associations with other families and institutions, in order to fulfill the family's role suitably and effectively, as well as to protect the rights, foster the good and represent the interests of the family 45 . b) Must the role of families be recognized? On the economic, social, juridical and cultural levels, the rightful role of families and family associations must be recognized in the planning and development of programs which touch on family life 46 . Article 9 Do families have the right to an adequate family policy? Families have the right to be able to rely on an adequate family policy on the part of public authorities in the juridical, economic, social and fiscal domains, without any discrimination whatsoever 47 . a) Do families have the right to dignified economic conditions? Families have the right to economic conditions which assure them a standard of living appropriate to their dignity and full development. They should not be impeded from acquiring and maintaining private possessions which would favor stable family life; and the laws concerning inheritance or transmission of property must respect the needs and rights of family members 48 . b) Do families have the right to social security? Families have the right to measures in the social domain which take into account their needs, especially in the event of the premature death of one or both parents, of the abandonment of one of the spouses, of accident, sickness or invalidity, in the case of unemployment, or whenever the family has to bear extra burdens on behalf of its members for reasons of old age, physical or mental handicaps, or the education of children 49 . c) Do elderly persons have rights? The elderly have the right to find within their own family or, when this is not possible, in suitable institutions, an environment which will enable them to live their later years of life in serenity while pursuing those activities which are compatible with their age and which enable them to participate in social life 50 . d) Do the families of prisoners have rights? The rights and needs of the family, and especially the value of family unity, must be taken into consideration in penal legislation and policy, in such a way that a detainee remains in contact with his or her family and that the family is adequately sustained during the period of detention. Part VI Article 10 Do families have the right to live together? Families have a right to a social and economic order in which the organization of work permits the members to live together, and does not hinder the unity, well-being, health and stability of the family, while offering also the possibility of wholesome recreation 51 . a) Must remuneration for work be sufficient? Remuneration for work must be sufficient for establishing and maintaining a family with dignity, either through a suitable salary, called a “family wage,” or through other social measures such as family allowances or the remuneration of the work in the home of one of the parents; it should be such that mothers will not be obliged to work outside the home to the detriment of family life and especially of the education of the children. b) Must the work of the homemaker be recognized? The work of the mother in the home must be recognized and respected because of its value for the family and for society 52 . Article 11 Does the family have the right to decent housing? The family has the right to decent housing, fitting for family life and commensurate to the number of the members, in a physical environment that provides the basic services for the life of the family and the community 53 . Article 12 Do the families of immigrants have the same rights? The families of migrants have the right to the same protection as that accorded other families 54 . a) Do they have a right to their culture? The families of immigrants have the right to respect for their own culture and to receive support and assistance towards their integration into the community to whose well-being they contribute. b) Do immigrants have the right to live united with their family? Emigrant workers have the right to see their family united as soon as possible. c) Do refugees have the right to be united with their family? Refugees have the right to the assistance of public authorities and international organizations in facilitating the reunion of their families. Conclusion Today the Christian family, founded on marriage, which is an image and a sharing in the covenant of love between Christ and the Church, will make manifest to all the living presence of the Savior in the world and the genuine nature of the Church, both by the love, generous fruitfulness, unity and fidelity of the spouses, and by the loving cooperation of all its members 55 . “Go into the whole world and teach all families the gospel of eternal salvation, which is the “gospel of families” 56 . Formula of perpetual vows in the IVE

Formula of perpetual consecration in the institute of the incarnate word 1 For love of the Father , first origin and supreme end of consecrated life; of Christ , who calls us to his intimacy; of the Holy Spirit , who disposes the soul to welcome his inspirations. I, N.N., freely make to God the oblation of my whole being: to deepen, with an ever more sincere and intense love, the gift of the evangelical counsels in their Trinitarian dimension; to be a concrete trace that the Trinity leaves in history, so that all men may discover the attraction and the longing for divine beauty; so that my life may be a living memorial of the way of existing and acting of Jesus, the Word made flesh (cf. Jn 1:14), before the Father and before men. Therefore, I commit all my strength not to shy away from the missionary adventure, to inculturate the Gospel in the diversity of all cultures, to prolong the Incarnation of the Word “in every man, in the whole man and in all the manifestations of man,” assuming all that is authentically human, to be like another humanity of Christ, to carry out with greater perfection the service of God and of men. For this reason, before God our Lord and all his saints, before N.N., Provincial Superior of the Institute of the Incarnate Word, (or: before N.N., who acts in place of the Provincial Superior of the Institute of the Incarnate Word) and in the presence of the members of this Institute and of the Servants of the Lord and the Virgin of Matará, I vow to live forever chaste , for the Kingdom of Heaven, poor , showing that God is the only true wealth of man, and obedient , unto death on a cross, so as to follow more intimately the Incarnate Word in his chastity, poverty and obedience, according to the evangelical way laid out in the Constitutions of the Institute of the Incarnate Word, and in order to do this better I make a fourth vow of consecration to Mary in maternal slavery of love . I ask the intercession of Our Lady, of the Twelve Apostles and of the other patron saints, the prayers of my brothers in the Incarnate Word and of the sisters of the Institute of the Servants of the Lord and the Virgin of Matará. May the love and grace of the Most Holy Trinity help me to be faithful in the work it has begun. The one receiving the vows responds: In the name of the Church and of the Institute of the Incarnate Word I receive with great joy into our Religious Family these brothers with perpetual vows, who have expressed the explicit desire for a total conformation with Christ, the Incarnate Word. Notes 1 Taken from the Constitutions , 257.
Golden Rose to Our Lady of Luján

“A shoot shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and from his root a flower shall blossom.” (Is 11:1) The Blessed Virgin of Luján is the Mother, Queen and principal Intercessor of our Religious Family of the Incarnate Word. For, as we have always been taught, She is the fruitful earth where the divine dew has engendered each of the vocations of our Religious Family. And since “vocation is love that can only be repaid with love” 1 , today we wish to present at the feet of our Mother, the Virgin of Luján, as a perpetual testimony of our love and gratitude for the vocations that She sends to our Religious Family, this Golden Rose, which is at the same time our vote of confidence (or, as it were, payment in advance) for the many vocations that we hope to conceive through her intercession and for which we already thank her. The Rose is 45 cm tall; it is made of silver and plated –inside and out– in 24-carat gold. All of it has been chiseled by hand , a detail that lets us glimpse God’s most personal call to souls. It is a rose with thorns , symbolizing that following Christ implies an intimate association with the Cross. And more notably, it is a rose with a bud . We wanted it so because it represents two things: the most sacred mystery of the Incarnation, which identifies us; and, on the other hand, the Mystical Rose in whom the divine dew engendered the bud of each of the vocations of our Religious Family. It has 7 leaves , above which the precious flower rises gracefully, expressing the sincere pursuit of holiness that is asked of each one of us and of the vocations we trust Our Lady will send us. For St. Bonaventure said that “whoever desires to obtain the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit, let him seek the flower on the stem. Through the stem let him reach the flower, and through the flower let him reach God” 2 . That is, let him seek Jesus in Mary, as the fundamental code of our spirituality says 3 , since through the stem we will reach the flower and through the flower we will find God. In this our fourth Marian vow is also made manifest, since, as our Constitutions admirably state: “Mary is ‘the proximate end, the mysterious center and the easy means of going to Christ’” 4 . In the petals of the rose go also our prayers asking for the perseverance, fidelity and holiness of our vocations. And finally, this rose has been made with material from Argentina and by an Argentine goldsmith, for that is the nation where She chose to stay and from which she has sent missionaries to so many places 5 . Prayer [At the moment of placing the rose at the feet of Our Lady:] Receive, O most worthy Queen and Mother of ours, this Golden Rose that we, your children of the Religious Family of the Incarnate Word, present to you today, as a gift of perpetual gratitude for the vocations with which you bless our Institutes and as a trusting pledge of the many more that we hope to conceive through your intercession. O most pure and Immaculate Conception of Luján, may the most pure dew of your grace make fruitful in countless souls the ardent desire to consecrate themselves to your Son in this Family of the Incarnate Word, so that, going to the ends of the earth, they may give off the fragrance of your perfume, which is nothing other than peace, joy and hope. Notes 1 Fr. Carlos Buela, IVE, Juan Pablo Magno , Ch. 31. 2 St. Alphonsus Maria de Liguori, The Glories of Mary , ch. 5, I. 5. 3 Directory of Spirituality, 325. 4 Constitutions , 88 ; op. cit . St. Louis Marie Grignion de Montfort, Treatise on True Devotion , 265. 5 Cf. Fr. Carlos Buela, IVE, María de Luján – El misterio de la Mujer que espera , ch. 12.
Consecration of an IVE Parish to Our Lady of Luján

Download PDF Originally used for the Consecration of St. Jerome Parish (Bronx, NY, USA) Formula of consecration of an IVE Parish to the Blessed Virgin of Luján O Blessed Virgin of Luján, powerful mediatrix between God and men, through whose hands come to us from Heaven all the favors and benefits we obtain, moved by your maternal tenderness and your ever-immense compassion, today we gather before your throne to express our love to you and to honor you as good children do their mothers. Most Holy Virgin of Luján! Evangelizer of all peoples, and Queen of the Institute of the Incarnate Word, to which you were pleased to entrust the mission in this parish. On this solemn day, inspired by the most sweet gentleness with which you bend down toward us, we, your faithful of the Parish [ name of the parish ], draw near to You, and before the whole heavenly court we wish to consecrate to you in perpetuity our entire Parish, with all its families, with all our children and young people, with all its married couples, with all its elderly and sick, with all its priests and religious sisters, with all the religious and priestly vocations that, through your intercession and for You, we would like to see flourish among us, with all its poor and its professionals, and all its good enterprises and institutions, present and future. Mother of the Incarnate Word, Immaculate Virgin Mary, You who one day willed to remain immovably among us: Look upon us, beloved Mother; here are your children. Through You , most sweet Lady, with You , in full union with your intentions and for You , we, your children of the Parish [ name of the parish ], wish from this day forward to live to honor and glorify you, and so fulfill the most sweet duty of loving you in time and for all eternity. O Virgin of Luján, she of the sky-blue and white mantle, keep in your suppliant hands all the souls here present, those who are no longer with us and those who will come after us. We beg you, Virgin Queen of our Parish and of our lives: convert sinners, dry the tears of those who suffer, relieve the poor, help families wounded by violence, lies and selfishness; guard the flower of purity of these your children and young people; increase the love of spouses, so that they may always walk in the light of your Son; strengthen in faith the catechists and the laity of our parish, so that they may be ever more committed and available for the service of the Gospel; raise up among us abundant vocations to the priesthood and to consecrated life, who will hold as their most sublime office the guiding of many other souls to the love of your Divine Son; may all the priests who pass through here always be “true servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.” And finally, beloved Mother, grant that all of us together, under the protection of your precious help and example, may work united and without rest to plant the Gospel of the beatitudes, and be authentic apostles of the evangelization of culture. Here we are, Blessed Virgin of Luján, from today and forever all the faithful of the Parish [ name of the parish ] are your happy servants. To You we belong irrevocably. Missionary of Heaven, bless us and bless all our works of apostolate which, for the glory of the Incarnate Word and through your intercession, we trust we may be able to carry out. † A. M. D. G.
Golden Rose to Our Lady of Luján – Tajikistan

Text delivered at the moment of presenting a golden rose at the feet of Our Lady of Luján in Tajikistan on the occasion of an anniversary of the missio sui iuris. Presentation of the Golden Rose to Our Lady of Luján [Introductory words] On this solemn day on which we celebrate yet another anniversary of the creation of the Missio Sui Iuris , before Fr. Pedro López, Superior of the missio , and the parishioners of St. Joseph Parish, we wish to offer the Blessed Virgin this golden rose as a sign of perpetual gratitude for her maternal intercession on account of the immense gift that the creation of the missio has meant for the Institute and for the whole Church in this blessed nation, and to implore her to be pleased to make it grow, making the grace of God fruitful in families and raising up in this small portion of the Church many vocations who, with “missionary zeal” 1 , will proclaim to the world “the Gospel that saves” 2 . [Prayer at the moment of the presentation] Our Lady of Luján,/ chosen from all eternity to be Mother of the Eternal Word, / and Heavenly Patroness of this nation,/ we –your children– belong to you without reserve, / and today we wish to leave at your blessed feet/ this golden rose/ as a filial gift and an expression of perpetual gratitude/ for the immeasurable gift of having entrusted to the Institute the care of your flock in these blessed lands. / May this rose be in turn a sign of the trusting and unceasing prayer/ that we place in your hands, invoking your favor,/ so that you may grant to your people in Tajikistan/ numerous priestly and religious vocations / who will wish to consecrate their lives/ “to prolonging the Incarnation of the Word in every man, / in the whole man/ and in all the manifestations of man” 3 ./ Queen of Tajikistan,/ flower without thorns, / blue lily of the valleys, / may the most pure dew of your grace/ make fruitful in the souls of your Tajik people the Gospel preached by the missionaries of this your little Family of the Incarnate Word; / may your unconditional Fiat to the will of the Father/ always find an echo in their hearts and, / may each day, / all of us and those who will come after us, / always find ourselves united, sheltered beneath your maternal mantle. / Most pure Mother of Luján, kindly accept this golden rose as a gift of gratitude for the wonders that the Almighty has worked through your mediation in the hearts of so many faithful who venerate you in this your maternal home. Notes 1 Constitutions , 231 . 2 Directory of Evangelization of Culture , 240. 3 Constitutions , 254 ;257.
Proper texts for the celebration of the Mass of St. Louis Marie

Download PDF St. Louis Mary Grignion de Montfort – April 28 ENTRANCE ANTIPHON How lovely upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who proclaims victory and says: City of Zion, your God now reigns. Alleluia COLLECT Lord God, who deigned to lead Saint Louis Mary, priest, along the way of salvation and of the love of Christ in the company of Most Holy Mary, grant us, by his example, that, meditating on the mysteries of divine love, we may devote ourselves tirelessly to the building up of your Church. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Or: Almighty and eternal God, who made Saint Louis Mary, priest, an outstanding witness and teacher of complete self-giving to Christ, your Son, through Mary, his Mother, grant that we, following this spiritual way, may contribute to the spread of your kingdom in the world. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. PRAYER OVER THE OFFERINGS Accept, O Lord, the offering of our priestly service on the feast of Saint Louis Mary, and grant that, freed from the cares and selfishness of this world, we may fully glorify your holy and glorious name. Through Jesus Christ our Lord PREFACE V. The Lord be with you. R. And with your spirit V. Lift up your hearts R. We lift them up to the Lord V. Let us give thanks to the Lord our God R. Liturgy of the Word First Reading (1 Cor 2:1-10) A reading from the first letter of the apostle St. Paul to the Corinthians Brothers: When I came to your city to proclaim the Gospel to you, I did not seek to do so by means of eloquent speech or human wisdom, but resolved to speak to you of nothing but Jesus Christ, and more than that, of Jesus Christ crucified. When I spoke to you and preached the Gospel to you, I did not wish to persuade you with the words of a wise man; on the contrary, I persuaded you by means of the Spirit and the power of God, so that your faith might rest on the power of God and not on the wisdom of men. For the Pope, the bishops, priests and deacons: that they may proclaim the Gospel of truth and joy, giving joyful witness to their vocation, let us pray to the Lord. 2. For the Salesians and the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians: that, imitating St. John Bosco in the total gift of his life to the service of the young, they may know how to form in them the true image of Christ, let us pray to the Lord. 3. For all who work in the Christian education of the young: that they may see in their holy patron a teacher and guide from whom to draw inspiration for their mission, let us pray to the Lord. 5. But the Lord intervened; he came to meet him. Peter turned to Him and asked: “ Quo vadis, Domine ?: Where are you going, Lord?” And the Lord answered him at once: “I am going to Rome to be crucified a second time.” Peter went back to Rome and stayed here until his crucifixion. Our time invites us, urges us and obliges us to look to the Lord and to immerse ourselves in a humble and devout meditation on the mystery of the supreme power of Christ himself. He who was born of the Virgin Mary, the Son of the carpenter – as he was thought to be –, the Son of the living God, as Peter confessed, came to make all of us “a kingdom of priests.” The Second Vatican Council has reminded us of the mystery of this power and of the fact that the mission of Christ – Priest, Prophet-Teacher, King – continues in the Church. All, the whole People of God, share in this threefold mission. And perhaps in the past the tiara, that triple crown, was placed on the Pope’s head to express, by means of such a symbol, the Lord’s plan for his Church, namely, that the whole hierarchical order of the Church of Christ, all the “sacred power” exercised in it, is nothing other than service, a service with a single aim: that the whole People of God share in this threefold mission of Christ and always remain under the power of the Lord, which has its origin not in the powers of this world but in the heavenly Father and in the mystery of the cross and of the resurrection. The absolute and yet gentle and sweet power of the Lord responds to what is deepest in man, to his loftiest aspirations of intellect, will and heart. This power does not speak with the language of force but expresses itself in charity and in truth. The new Successor of Peter in the See of Rome today raises a fervent, humble and trusting prayer: O Christ! Make me become, and be, a servant of your unique power! A servant of your gentle power! A servant of your power that knows no setting! Make me a servant! Indeed, the servant of your servants. Brothers and sisters! Do not be afraid to welcome Christ and to accept his power! Help the Pope and all who wish to serve Christ and, with the power of Christ, to serve man and the whole of humanity! Do not be afraid! Open, and even more, open wide the doors to Christ! Open to his saving power the boundaries of States, economic and political systems, the vast fields of culture. of civilization and of development. Do not be afraid! Christ knows “what is in man.” He alone knows it! So often man today does not know what he carries within, in the depths of his soul, of his heart. Many times he feels unsure about the meaning of his life in this world. He feels overcome by doubt that turns into despair. Allow, then – I beg you, I implore you with humility and with trust – allow Christ to speak to man. He alone has words of life, yes, of eternal life! Responsory R. Do not be afraid: the Redeemer of man has revealed the power of the cross and has given his life for us. * Open wide the doors to Christ . V. In the Church we are called to share in his power. * Open wide the doors to Christ. Prayer O God, rich in mercy, who willed that St. John Paul II, pope, should guide your whole Church, we ask that, instructed by his teachings, you grant us to open our hearts with confidence to the saving grace of Christ, the sole Redeemer of man. Who lives and reigns. Liturgy of the Hours Saints Pedro, a diocesan priest and founder of the Teresian Association, and Inocencio of the Immaculate, a Passionist religious, head the multitude of saints and blesseds – bishops, priests, consecrated persons and laity – who gave to Christ the supreme testimony of love, martyred in hatred of the faith in Spain between 1931 and 1939, during the religious persecution against the Church. (Sermon 335, 1-2: PL 38, 1470) The meaning of martyrdom Since this is the feast of the holy martyrs, what better can we speak of than their glory? May the Lord of the martyrs help us, since he is their crown. A short while ago we heard the blessed apostle Paul proclaiming the cry of the martyrs themselves: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Such is the cry of the martyrs. Tribulation? Distress? Persecution? Hunger? Nakedness? Dangers? The sword? For it is written: “For your sake we are put to death all the day long and counted as sheep for the slaughter.” But in all these things we conquer through him who loved us . This is the cry of the martyrs: to bear everything, not to presume on themselves, and to love the One who is glorified in his own, so that whoever boasts may boast in the Lord . They also knew what we sang a short while ago: Rejoice in the Lord and exult, you just . If the just rejoice in the Lord, the unjust know how to rejoice only in the world. But this is the first army to be overcome: first pleasure must be overcome, and then pain. How can someone overcome the cruelty of the world who is unable to overcome its flatteries? This world flatters by promising honors, riches, pleasure; this world threatens by making use of pain, poverty and humiliation. Whoever does not despise what it promises, how can he overcome its threats? Riches bring their own delight; who does not know it? But justice has a greater delight still. The Apostle certainly passed over all the flatteries of the world, and he wanted you, the one flattered by the world, to call them to mind. Why? Because he was announcing in advance the combats of the martyrs: those combats in which they overcame persecution, hunger, thirst, want, dishonor and, finally, the fear of death and the cruelest of enemies. But consider, brothers, that all of it is the work of Christ’s art. The Apostle invites us to prefer the love of Christ to the love of the world. How many hardships must those endure who wish to steal what belongs to others? Persecution ? Not even persecution breaks them. The miser says in his heart what perhaps he does not dare to say with his tongue: Who separates us from the craving for gold? Tribulation? Distress? Persecution? The misers too can say to gold: “For your sake we are led to death day by day.” Rightly, then, do the holy martyrs say in the psalm: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from that of wicked people . Distinguish, he said, my tribulation, for the misers also suffer tribulations. Distinguish my distress, for the misers also suffer it. Distinguish my persecutions, for the misers also suffer them. Distinguish my hunger, for, provided they acquire gold, the misers also suffer it. Distinguish my nakedness, for the misers too let themselves be stripped for gold. Distinguish my death, for the misers too die for gold. What does it mean: Distinguish my cause ? For your sake we are led to death day by day . They suffer all that for gold; we, for you. The punishment is the same, but the cause is different. If the cause is different, the victory is assured. Therefore, if we look to their cause, we will love these feasts of the martyrs. Let us love in them not their sufferings but the cause of those sufferings; for if we love only their sufferings, we will find many who suffer worse things for evil causes. But let us look at the cause; look at the cross of Christ: there was Christ, and there were the thieves. The punishment was the same, but the cause was different. One thief believed, the other blasphemed. The Lord, as at a tribunal, acted as judge for both: the one who blasphemed he sent to hell; the other he took with him to paradise. Why this? Because, although the punishment was the same, the cause of each was different. Choose, then, the causes of the martyrs if you want to attain the palm of the martyrs. Responsory cf. Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. * Thus you will be. The prayer as at Lauds. Lauds Benedictus, ant. An innumerable multitude of martyrs persevered in fraternal love, because they had one spirit and one faith. Proper Prayers Mass in honor of SAINT JOSÉ GABRIEL DEL ROSARIO BROCHERO March 16 SAINT JOSÉ GABRIEL DEL ROSARIO BROCHERO Priest The Cura Brochero was born on March 16, 1840, near Villa Santa Rosa (Province of Córdoba). At 16 he entered the Major Seminary of Córdoba, “Our Lady of Loreto,” where he received his priestly formation, and he pursued his philosophical and theological studies at the University of Córdoba. He was ordained a priest on November 4, 1866. A typical feature of his priestly life was his presentation of the Gospel in vivid language, close to the understanding of simple people. His concern was to enlighten the life of his faithful from the Word of God, not in a general and abstract way but applied to the concrete circumstances of life. He was appointed Pastor of Villa del Tránsito (today Villa Cura Brochero), from where he carried out his intense pastoral ministry. He died there, sick with leprosy and blind, on January 26, 1914, at the age of 74. Directory of Evangelization of Culture

Introduction The evangelization of cultures is the specific end of our Institute 1 . In particular, in the present context of relativism and cultural pluralism in a globalized world, there is a special urgency to carry out the work of inculturation. That is, on the one hand there emerge the challenges of cultural relativism and de-Christianization, principally in countries of ancient Christian tradition. On the other hand, the Gospel comes into contact with cultural areas until now outside the range of Christianity's radiance, especially among the peoples of Africa and, even more, of Asia, in which there exists a plurality of ancient cultural and religious traditions that opens new tasks for inculturation 2 . Nevertheless, inculturation constitutes, above all, an intrinsic requirement of evangelization 3 . For this reason, t he Christianity of the third millennium must respond ever better to this requirement of inculturation 4 . Culture in general 1. Its essence 2. First of all, we must have a clear idea of the nature of culture. The noun culture derives from the Latin verb colo ( colo , colis , colere ), which means to cultivate. Thus, etymologically, by culture we designate the essence and art of cultivating the field. It implies –as can be noted in the words agriculture, pisciculture, apiculture, etc.– a process or activity directed toward obtaining better fruits from nature. 3. From this first sense it came to signify, metaphorically, cultivation in man himself and in all his human dimensions; that is, a second form of cultivation, immanent to man, an activity –intelligent and free– directed immediately to the perfection of man himself, through the unfolding of all his powers in harmony with his true nature. It is a matter of the cultivation of the whole man, body and soul, in a harmonious hierarchy. Cicero called it cultura animi . Thus, culture has a markedly personal sense. But it also has –and today this is predominant– a social sense, including in its meaning all the achievements of man as a social being 5 . It is a collective tradition that informs the life of all individuals. We can then speak of Hellenic, medieval, Spanish, Argentine culture, etc. 4. This culture in the social sense Fr. Meinvielle calls civilization, distinguishing it from culture in the personal sense: “although the connections between them are great, they cannot be considered identical. Culture… would seem to indicate the activity of man applied to human nature so that it may yield the fruits of which it is capable… it connotes preferably the perfecting of the human personality, while civilization looks first to that of society. We would say, then, that man seeks his culture in civilization; to signify that culture arises as a conquest of the free and personal effort of man, achieved with the help of civilization, which has provided the means to attain it” 6 . In this latter sense it can further be pointed out that civilization, in its deepest meaning, belongs rather to human culture, since it responds to the spiritual and moral needs of man 7 . 5. St. John Paul II, uniting both senses –the personal and the social–, defines culture as the “manifestation of man as a person, as a community, as a people and a nation” 8 . We have, then, that culture is that particular way in which men and peoples cultivate their relationship with nature and with their brothers, with themselves and with God, in order to attain a fully human existence 9 . Hence it can in a certain way be said that man, through his intellect and freedom, is the creator, in a broad sense, of a better world, built upon the natural world; that is, he can transform natural beings and his own being, perfecting them. Thus, for example, a man through study acquires the habit or perfection of science, or through the practice of the virtues becomes an honest man 10 . 6. St. Thomas, commenting on Aristotle, says that “the human race lives by art and reason” 11 .
