And united to it, the example and witness of life: “Where there is faith, prayer, charity, apostolate, Christian life, there the gifts of God are multiplied” 380 , for “the religious and priests who serenely live their vocation day by day, faithful to the commitments they have made, humble and hidden builders of the Kingdom of God, from whose words, behavior and life the luminous joy of the choice they made radiates… are precisely… those who by their example will spur many on to welcome into their hearts the charism of vocation” 381 . Hence every counter-witness, every inconsistency between how values or ideals are expressed and how they are actually lived, every seeking of oneself and not of the Kingdom of God and his justice 382 , every falsification of the word of God 383 , “are frequently strong obstacles for those who feel the call of Christ: come and follow me …” 384 . h) In the three white things 385 The Eucharist Ecclesial communion has its root and its center in the Holy Eucharist. It is the source and creative power of communion among the members of the Church because it unites each one with Christ himself: “Really sharing in the Body of the Lord in the breaking of the Eucharistic Bread, we are taken up into communion with Him and with one another, because the bread is one, we are one in a single body, for we all partake of that one bread (1 Cor 10:17)” 386 . In the Eucharist “the whole spiritual common good of the Church is substantially contained” 387 ; “this is Christ” 388 . The Church is the Body of Christ. This means that the Eucharist, in which the Lord gives his Body and transforms us into one Body 389 , is the place where the Church permanently expresses herself in her most essential form: present everywhere and at the same time one , just as Christ is one. In the Eucharist every member of the faithful finds himself in his Church, since in every valid celebration of the Eucharist the One, Holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church becomes present, and this regardless of whether or not he belongs, from the canonical point of view, to the diocese, parish or particular community where the celebration takes place. The communion of the particular Churches in the universal Church –besides faith, Baptism and the Episcopate– is founded above all on the Eucharist. For the Eucharistic Sacrifice never belongs to one community alone, since that community receives, with the Lord, the complete gift of salvation, and is thus manifested –beyond its visible particularity– as the image and true presence of the One, Holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church 390 . The oneness and indivisibility of the Eucharistic Body of the Lord implies the oneness and indivisibility of his Mystical Body. From every Eucharist there arises the giving of oneself to the Lord by being inserted into his one and undivided Body. For this reason, the Petrine ministry, the foundation of the unity of the Episcopate and of the universal Church, corresponds profoundly to the Eucharistic dimension of the Church. The unity of the Eucharist and the unity of the Episcopate “with Peter and under Peter” 391 are not independent roots of the unity of the Church because, by the institution of Christ himself, Eucharist and Episcopate are essentially linked realities 392 . The Episcopate is one, just as the Sacrifice of the one Lord is one. The liturgy manifests this reality, since every Eucharist is celebrated in union with one’s own bishop, with the Pope, with the universal Episcopate, with the clergy and with all the members of the People of God 393 . Every valid celebration of the Eucharist expresses this universal communion with Peter and with the whole Church, or objectively calls for it, as in the Churches separated from Rome. This being so, we will always find the deepest foundation of our unity as a Religious Family in the Eucharist, which perpetuates the Sacrifice of the Cross. It must be one of our great loves, since it is the unmistakable sign of God’s measureless love for men, of God who wishes to remain among men, of God who gives himself totally to man: “In the Eucharist, the logic of the Incarnation reaches its ultimate consequences” 394 . The principal act of the priest is sacrifice, and the sacrifice “of praise,” “pure, immaculate and holy” 395 , “pleasing… and salvation for the whole world” 396 , which “opens the way for us” to the Father 397 , “unique” 398 , “of perfect reconciliation” 399 , “ours” 400 , “living” 401 . That is why in the Eucharistic Liturgy Christ speaks, above all, with the power of his Sacrifice. It is a very concise and, at the same time, ardent discourse. We must know how to listen to it attentively. Every month let one Holy Mass be offered in suffrage for the deceased members, another for the intentions of the Superior General, and another asking for all the members of our Institutes the grace of final perseverance. The Virgin Mary The Virgin Mary must be another of our great loves. Because of her union with Christ and with the Church. Because she begot us, the members, together with the Head. Because she was given to us as Mother when she was standing at the foot of the Cross: Behold your son (Jn 19:26). The Blessed Virgin Mary is the model of ecclesial communion “in the order of faith, charity and perfect union with Christ” 402 ; She “is the image and beginning of the Church… she shines forth before the pilgrim People of God as a sign of sure hope and of consolation” 403 . She is in the midst of the Apostles, in the very heart of the nascent Church: they persevered with one accord in prayer with some women, with Mary, the Mother of Jesus, and with his brothers (Acts 1:14), and of the Church of all times. Indeed, “the Church was gathered in the upper room (of the Cenacle) with Mary, who was the Mother of Jesus, and with his brothers. One cannot, therefore, speak of the Church unless Mary, the Mother of the Lord, is present with his brothers” 404 . The Marian dimension is essential to the one Church of Christ, just as the Eucharistic dimension and the Petrine dimension are essential to her. We must be Apostles of Mary, giving ourselves to Her in the maternal slavery of love and doing everything “through Mary, with Mary, in Mary and for Mary” 405 . In times of eutrapelia let there always be some remembrance of the Blessed Virgin. Let the same be done when cultural activities take place, since after Jesus Christ no one does as much for the evangelization of culture as our Mother in heaven. The Pope Our third great love must always be the white figure of the Pope: “Where Peter is, there is the Church” 406 and “Peter speaks through the mouth of Leo” 407 . After Simon bore witness to Christ: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God (Mt 16:16), Christ bore witness to Simon: You are Peter and upon this rock I will build my Church (Mt 16:18). The idea of a Body of the Churches calls for the existence of a Head of the Churches, which is precisely the Church of Rome, which “presides over the universal communion of charity” 408 . The Successor of Peter “is the perpetual and visible principle and foundation” 409 of the unity of the universal Church and of the unity of the Episcopate. Hence the Petrine ministry is not a service that reaches the particular Churches “from outside,” but one “already belonging to the essence of each particular Church from within” 410 . The ministry of the Primacy entails an episcopal power, that is, as universal bishop and bishop of the diocese of Rome, which is not a mere dignity, so that everything a bishop can do in his parishes the Pope can do in each and every one of the particular Churches of the world; it is supreme power, no one else possesses equal or greater power; it is full power, not only the principal part; it is immediate, he can exercise it over bishops and faithful; it is universal, over all without excluding any; it is ordinary, derived directly from Jesus Christ; and “he can always exercise it freely” 411 . The primordial task of the Roman Pontiff for the whole Church is the promotion of unity, which is not at odds with the promotion of the diversification proper to communion. We make our own the teaching of St. Ignatius of Loyola: “To be right in everything, we must always hold that the white that I see, I will believe to be black, if the Hierarchical Church so determines it” 412 . Therefore, certain that this is the will of Jesus Christ, “let us remain deaf when someone speaks to us leaving the Pope aside, or not explicitly in favor of the Pope and of the sound and exact doctrine of the Church: such people are not a planting of the Heavenly Father, but evil offshoots of heresies that produce deadly fruit” 413 . Let us always remember that “the Pope must be loved on the cross; and whoever does not love him on the cross does not truly love him. To be with the Pope in everything means to be with God in everything; to love Jesus Christ and to love the Pope is the same love” 414 , since “… to love the Pope, to love the Church, is to love Jesus Christ” 415 . Article 6: His second Coming a) Prior signs Just as Jesus Christ came the first time in humility and poverty, he is to come a second time, but in power and majesty, because he will come to call to account and to pass sentence; that is why he will come in greatness and dignity. The major signs of his second Coming are three: a) The Gospel will be preached to the whole world 416 . b) There will be a universal apostasy 417 . c) The Antichrist will make his appearance 418 . There will be, therefore, a time when men will turn away from the truth and take pleasure in iniquity 419 , a time in which the majority will not have authentic faith in Jesus Christ. The certainty that one day this universal apostasy will occur must lead us not to hitch ourselves to the triumphal chariot of any movement or ideology that is established apart from Christ, even if it seems that the whole world follows it. We must always follow Christ. And even if the enemies seem to be the majority we must say: “we are surrounded on all sides; let’s not let them escape.” For “to the soul that contemplates God every creature becomes small” 420 . b) The final and universal resurrection Toward the end the resurrection of the flesh will take place. All men and women are to rise by the power of God. We believe in the resurrection and we are not afraid of the executioners who lie in wait for the Church in every age: do not be afraid of those who kill the body, for they cannot kill the soul (Mt 10:28). The time of this resurrection is hidden, and “all who until now have striven to determine that time have been held to be liars” 421 . The soul will take up its same body, whole, and will enjoy the endowments of impassibility, subtlety, agility and clarity or beauty. How great must be our confidence and joy in knowing that death has already been conquered! And it has been conquered thanks to the Incarnation of the Word and to his redemptive Sacrifice. That is why the Incarnation of the Word is the condition and guarantee for the whole universe. “The source of life and of salvation from despair for all men, the condition ‘ sine qua non ’ and the guarantee for the whole universe are contained in the words ‘The Word became flesh’ and in ‘faith in these words’” 422 . For “the Incarnation of the Son of God is the foundation, the source and the model both of a new supernatural order of existence for all men, who precisely from this mystery obtain the grace that sanctifies and saves them, and of a Christian anthropology, which is projected also into the natural sphere of thought and life with its exaltation of man as a person, placed at the center of society and –one may say– of the whole world” 423 . c) The Parousia and the final Judgment Then the Parousia of the Lord will take place: The hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice (Jn 5:28); Then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty (Lk 21:27); The sign (the sign of the Cross) of the Son of Man will appear in the sky (Mt 24:30). At that moment the universal Judgment will take place. Christ, together with his elect: you also will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel (Mt 19:28), will separate the sheep from the goats; some he will place at his right, the others at his left, and he will say: Come, blessed of my Father, take possession of the Kingdom… (Mt 25:34) and Depart from Me, you cursed, go into the eternal fire (Mt 25:41). The wicked will go into eternal fire and the just into eternal life (Mt 25:46). We must become ever more convinced that we do not work for ephemeral or passing things, but “for the most divine work among the divine” 424 , the eternal salvation of souls and the glorious resurrection of bodies. On the one hand, we must say with St. Luigi Orione: “Place me, Lord, upon the mouth of hell, so that I, by your mercy, may close it” 425 ; and, on the other, know that we work for eternal life. d) The renewal Then the renewal of the whole material universe will take place, since there will be a new heaven and a new earth (Is 65:17; Rev 21:1), so that man, risen in glory, may see the divinity sensibly and in some way in bodies through manifest signs. It will be fully true: “heaven and earth and all that is contained in them, behold, they tell me from every side to love you…” 426 . How this renewal will be in quantity and manner “is known only to the one who will be its Author” 427 . There God will be all in all things (1 Cor 15:28), and matter will attain its highest dignity, expressing the Divine Spirit, for it will be a perfect mirror of God. All that is left to us is to pray, work and hope, knowing that the form of this world is passing away (1 Cor 7:31). CHAPTER 3: EPILOGUE We wish to end this part of our fundamental code by mentioning, in summary form, what we want our spirituality to be: Not Jesus or Mary; not Mary or Jesus. Neither Jesus without Mary, nor Mary without Jesus. Not only Jesus, but also Mary; nor only Mary, but also Jesus. Always Jesus and Mary; always Mary and Jesus. To Mary through Jesus: Behold your Mother (Jn 19:27). To Jesus through Mary: Do whatever He tells you (Jn 2:5). First, Jesus, the God-man; but then Mary, the Mother of God. He, the Head; She, the Neck; we, the Body. Everything through Jesus and through Mary; with Jesus and with Mary; in Jesus and in Mary; for Jesus and for Mary. In short, simply: Jesus and Mary; Mary and Jesus. And through Christ, to the Father, in the Holy Spirit.
